body.p: This responds to the Final Office Action dated June 18, 2024.
Claims 1 and 16 are presently amended. No claims are presently canceled and no claims are presently added. As a result, claims 1-20 remain pending in this application.

p.u: Request for Consideration Under 37 C.F.R. 1.116(b) After Final Consideration Pilot 2.0

body.p: Applicant respectfully requests consideration under 37 C.F.R. 1.116(b) under the After Final Consideration Pilot (AFCP) 2.0. A completed form PTO/SB/434 is included herewith. This is the first and only request under AFCP 2.0 filed in response to the outstanding final rejection. The response includes an amendment to an independent claim, and the amendment does not broaden the scope of the independent claims in any aspect.
Applicant believes that the remaining issues in this application are amenable to resolution
through this program. Applicant is willing and available to participate in any interview requested by the Examiner concerning the present response.

The undersigned would like to thank Examiner Nicole F. Johnson for the courtesy of a telephone interview on August 21, 2024. Applicant requested the interview to briefly discuss the Examiner's "broadest reasonable interpretation" (see Response to Arguments section of Final Office Action) of "producing the color output on the user interface to provide an indication of the sensed neural activity to a user" and to discuss a proposed clarifying amendment to clarify that color output is displayed on a user interface to provide a visual indication of the sensed neural activity to a user. Examiner Johnson understood the argued distinctions and indicated that further consideration would be needed. Examiner Johnson also suggested that Applicant clarify the patent subject matter eligibility of the claims.

Claim 1 was rejected on the ground of nonstatutory double patenting as being unpatentable over claim 12 of U.S. Patent No. 11,207,018. The Examiner is invited to call the undersigned attorney to request a terminal disclaimer at such time when the claims are otherwise found to be in condition for allowance.
Claims 1-20 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Wells (U.S. 2011/0295347) in view of Webb (U.S. 2007/0060984). Applicant respectfully traverses.

As identified in paragraph [0054] of the present application, certain neurostimulation systems may sense neural activity in a patient as an electrical waveform and may provide a graphical representation of the electrical waveform to a user. As illustrated by the neuron recording in FIG. 1B, such an electrical waveform may be complex (e.g., the electrical waveform may include pulses, bursts of pulses, trains of bursts, and sequences of pulses, bursts, and trains) and it may be difficult for the user to recognize patterns within the graphical representation. The electrical waveform may include a distribution of frequencies and amplitudes. The inventor has recognized, among other things, that it is possible to provide alternative representations of the measured neural activity, such as color representations. Thus, the present subject matter addresses the problem with interpreting complex electrical waveforms, such as sensed neural activity, to provide a user-perceivable output that may be easier to interpret than a graphical representation of an electrical waveform, such as the electrical waveform [0054] - [0057].

Wells is directed to optical nerve stimulation (e.g., Title, Abstract). Specific waveforms are purported to provide more specificity in the stimulation of the nerve (e.g., Wells at [0041], [0042], [0049], [0052]). Thus, Wells appears to purport to use different color pulses (e.g., yellow, blue pulses) to optically stimulate nerves. It appears that the rejection relies on the therapy applied to the patient as the output to the user interface. Applicant respectfully submits that one of ordinary skill in the art would not believe that the "optical stimulation" of the patient's nerve is a user interface.

Applicant has amended claims 1 and 16 to further clarify the distinction. For example, the color output is displayed on the user interface to provide a visual indication of the sensed neural activity to a user using the different colors corresponding to the different feature values.

Furthermore, Applicant has chosen to further clarify how the color is determined from the sensed neural activity. An electrical waveform is generated from the sensed neural activity. The waveform includes signal features with feature values. The color output is determined by transforming the feature values to the color output using a stored mapping function for mapping the feature values to the color output.
Applicant respectfully submits that the activity is not practically able to be performed by a human mind. The waveforms are complex (e.g., see neuron recording of FIG. 1B;[0054]-[0057])
such that it is difficult to recognize patterns within the waveform. The patterns cannot be practically performed by the human mind.

The present subject is a practical application that provides a technical improvement to medical devices by improving the user interface for sensed neural signals. Sensed neural activity is transformed into color representations where different colors represent different feature values.
For at least these reasons, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the rejection and reconsideration and allowance of the claims.

In the interest of clarity and brevity, every assertion made in the Office Action may not have been equally addressed. Silence regarding any such assertion does not constitute any admission or acquiescence. All rights not exercised in connection with this response, such as the right to challenge or rebut any tacit or explicit characterization of any reference or of any of the present claims or the right to challenge or rebut any asserted factual or legal basis of any of the rejections, are reserved.

It is respectfully submitted that the claims are in condition for allowance, and notification to that effect is earnestly requested. The Examiner is invited to telephone the undersigned at (612) 373-6900 to facilitate prosecution of this application.
